title: Introduce regional SLO safety-net and batch-aware graceful degrader
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a regional SLO safety-net controller and a batch-aware degrader that limits per-tenant burst tokens when regional latency or KV pressure rises. Improves graceful degradation and reduces SLO breaches during short regional overloads.
description:
Summary: Adds a lightweight regional safety-net controller that enforces an SLO backstop (max tolerated p99 latency and emergency token budget) and a batch-aware graceful degrader in the runtime request path. This change is targeted at short-lived regional overloads that previously caused cascading SLO violations; it provides an emergency, short-duration shed and a probabilistic admission reduction that preserves high-priority tenants and KV coherence.

Motivation & Context: Over the past quarter we observed a recurring pattern where transient KV pressure + routing imbalances produced p99 spikes for up to 30s in a single region (see ENG-5421). Existing circuit breakers tripped too late or evicted too broadly; autoscale is too slow to react for these bursts. We need a fast safety-net that: 1) enforces a short emergency token budget per-region, 2) applies batch-aware admission control to avoid breaking batching heuristics, and 3) prefers graceful quality degradation over wholesale evictions.

What changed (high-level):
- controlplane/slo_safety_net: new controller that monitors region-level latency/kv_backpressure metrics and computes an "emergency budget" window (short TTL, decay).
- runtime/degrader: batch-aware admission decorator that probabilistically reduces incoming admission for new requests while preserving active KV sessions and ongoing KV-prefetch flows. Uses sequence-length-aware probability scaling to avoid starving long-running streams.
- routing/geo: tie-breaker updated to prefer standby pools when safety-net is active and to annotate requests with safety-net trace tags for observability.
- telemetry: dashboards and a Telemetry event emitted when a safety-net window opens/closes; added histogram buckets for degraded vs normal request latency.

Performance and safety considerations:
- The degrader is deliberately conservative by default: feature flag disabled; when enabled the probability scaling is limited to avoid dropping >40% of eligible admissions for more than 10s.
- The controller uses rolling p50/p95/p99 telemetry with short windows to avoid noisy flips. It requires both latency and kv_backpressure signals to open a safety window.
- We added a short cooldown and exponential backoff for reopen attempts to prevent flapping.

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests cover degrader probability math, sequence-length scaling, and controller open/close thresholds.
- Integration tests simulate KV pressure and verify the safety-net opens and reduces admission while preserving active KV sessions.
- CI: all checks passed on merge (lint, unit, integration-canary, e2e-smoke).

Review conversation (abridged):
- Priya Nair (reviewer): "This addresses a lot of the pain from last month's incident. Two asks: 1) ensure telemetry tags are injected early enough so observability doesn't lose the 'pre-degrade' signal; 2) make the default decay parameters conservative in prod."
- Maya Chen (author): "Agree on both. Controller now emits a 'preflight' event when thresholds approach the open point; default decay set to 30s half-life and a max emergency budget of 10% of regional capacity unless overridden by ops."
- Diego Alvarez (reviewer): "Routing change looks safe, but add an integration test to ensure we don't re-route requests mid-kv-session. I added a suggested test harness in comments."
- Maya Chen: "Added tests and verified with local harness; routing change now tags requests and routing ensures in-flight preservation."
- Lars Mikkelsen (approver): "Small nit on log levels; otherwise LGTM. Please squash before merge."

CI checks: lint: pass; unit: pass; integration-canary: pass; e2e-smoke: pass; security-scan: pass.

Merge outcome: Merged via squash merge on 2026-02-23 by Lars Mikkelsen. Commit message: "slo(safety-net): add regional SLO safety-net controller and batch-aware degrader (ENG-5421)"

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag default: disabled for prod.
- Canary: enabled in canary clusters for 48h (completed).
- Gradual rollout: enable for 10% of regions for 24h, observe telemetry; increase to 50% after stability window; then enable globally.

Operational runbook pointers (docs/ops/slo-safety-net.md):
- How to temporarily disable safety-net per-region (ops-only toggle).
- How to read safety-net events and correlate with KV pressure dashboards.
- Steps for emergency rollback if safety-net causes unexpected throttling.

Notes for follow-ups:
- Consider exposing tenant-level override windows for enterprise customers who prefer stricter isolation.
- Add more nuanced batching compatibility for multi-tenant kernels (future work).
